about: The one table of the file formats exav handles. scripts/formats.mjs checks it against the code (the extractor's Format enum, Cargo features and streaming walkers, the scanner's FileType, the viewer's plugins and signatures) and writes from it the summary sentences in the docs and the viewer's extensions and types (crates/exav-viewer/ts/core/formats.generated.ts), and the reader module and crates of each format the extractor reads (formats/code.generated.json); the site's formats page (www/src/components/FormatTable.astro) reads both when the site is built. Fields: id; name; kind; ext (lower case, with the dot; matched with endsWith); mime (the types the viewer sniffs, the registered ones and the ones desktops and browsers give the format; the viewer claims every one of an entry that has a viewer, unless it also lists the type as one the extension answers over or as a container type); magic (alternatives, each a list of offset:hex that must all hold); detect {at, how}: where the detection of the format looks, and in one line a user reads how it tells the format. at is a place or a list of places, from: start (bytes at fixed offsets within the first 4 MiB of the file, as magic gives them), end (a record at the end of the file, or the last bytes read), after-image (the bytes after the image of a PE, where an installer keeps its data), string (a string searched for in the start, the extent in how), structure (places that a parsed structure names: a resource, a directory, a table, a chain of headers), content (what the first bytes of a text are like, no fixed bytes), name (the extension, or the type the host gives, and no bytes); scan {type: exav-core FileType::as_str or null, mode: container | reported | view | type | none}; unpack {format: exav-unpack Format variant, feature: Cargo feature or null, read: stream | members | whole | reported}; sniffs (types the viewer sniffs from the bytes without claiming them); viewer (the plugin that opens it, or null); note; spec (optional: the specification of the format from whoever defines it, or else the best public description of it, as an https URL, or for an entry that groups several formats a list of { url, title } in the order of the name, the title naming what the link is for). unpack.read is stream (members decoded as they are read), members (the container is read whole, its members stream out), whole, or reported (recognised, not decoded). The viewer's own test (ts/core/registry.test.ts) and the scanner's (tests/suites/format_registry.rs) read this file; the scanner's also runs the detector over a fixture of each format that has one, and checks that it reads the places detect.at names and none other.

scanModes.reported: recognised and reported UNSCANNABLE or PASSWORD-PROTECTED, not opened
scanModes.view: scanned through a text view as well as its bytes
scanModes.type: typed by its content, its signatures applied

formats.name: LZMA (.lzma)

detect.how: No magic. The first 14 bytes must be a header the LZMA tools would write (properties below 225, a dictionary size of 2^n or 3 x 2^(n-1), a size below 256 GiB or unknown, a zero byte to open the range coder) and the stream must start to decode.

formats.note: LZMA-alone, as LZMA Utils wrote it. No magic number: typed by the header's own rules (properties, dictionary size, size, first range-coder byte).

formats.name: Partition maps (GPT, APM, MBR) and raw disk images

detect.how: `EFI PART` at byte 512 (GPT), `ER` at the start and `PM` at byte 512 (Apple), or `55 AA` at byte 510 with a partition entry that fits the image and is not a FAT or NTFS boot sector (MBR).

A boot sector: a jump (`EB` or `E9`) first, a printable OEM name, a sector size of 512 to 4096, a power of two sectors per cluster, `55 AA` at byte 510, and `FAT` in the type field at byte 54 or `FAT32` at byte 82.
`NTFS` and four spaces at byte 3, a sector size of 512 to 4096 at byte 11, and `55 AA` at byte 510.
The superblock at byte 1024: `53 EF` at byte 1080 and the fields around it (block counts, groups, inodes, features) in agreement. Not tried on a PE or ELF.
`EXFAT` and three spaces at byte 3, zeros from byte 11 to 63, and `55 AA` at byte 510.
